message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and talked‑about crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A fresh take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending psychological terror with sci‑fi twists. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced style, witty dialogue, and a star‑packed ensemble keep the caper sharp. |
| 3 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic saga of organized crime, featuring De Niro’s groundbreaking de‑motion‑capture performance. |
| 4 | **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Whitehead | A chilling psychological thriller that blends supernatural dread with a deeply personal narrative. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A tense, character‑driven drama about a man falsely accused of child abuse, exploring paranoia and social media hysteria. |
| 6 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller, capturing the tension of the 1969 protest trial. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑thriller that reimagines the last sanctioned duel in France, with strong performances and period detail. |
| 8 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Zorion Eguileor, Iván Massagué | A dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict and human nature. |
| 9 | **The Lodge** | Severin Fiala & Veronika Franz | Riley Keough, Toni Collette | A psychological thriller that blurs reality and hallucination, delivering a tense, claustrophobic atmosphere. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** (TV series) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson‑Cohen | Though technically a TV series, it’s worth mentioning for its high‑quality crime‑thriller storytelling and strong character arcs. |

These titles cover a range of sub‑genres—from psychological thrillers and courtroom dramas to dystopian narratives—so you’ll find something that fits your taste whether you’re looking for cerebral tension, action‑packed capers, or socially‑relevant commentary. Happy watching!
